newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris prosecutor wants six jailed in BP tower sale.
newsitem.headline: Paris prosecutor wants six jailed in BP tower sale.

text.p: A French prosecutor on Thursday sought jail terms for six of 20 people on trial for alleged bribery in the sale of the French headquarters of British Petroleum in 1988.
The court has yet to reach any verdicts in the case, which centres on allegations that seven million francs ($1.23 million) was paid in illegal commissions during the sale.

Deputy state prosecutor Paulette Arrault requested the heaviest sentence, a five-year term, for Christian Schwartz, director of Patrimoine et Investissement, one of two companies that set up French property firm Paul Doumer in order to purchase BP Tower.
She sought jail terms of two years and 30 months respectiviely on Briton Clive Llewellyn and Frenchman Benoit Michelon, two executives of Feau-Hampton, a third company involved in the deal.

They are accused of paying corruption money to Paul Gatrill, a Briton who was responsible for BP's real estate. He is accused of pocketing one million francs ($175,000) in return for giving inside information to Feau-Hampton and unduly favouring the winning bidder over rivals.
Schwartz, Llewellyn and Michelon have all denied involvement in a bribery scheme.

Gatrill, 54, who quit BP in 1990, admitted in court earlier that he received the money from Feau-Hampton but said it was a payment for a survey he made on investment opportunities on the London property market.
Arrault asked for three other defendents to be jailed and said the rest should receive suspended sentences.

BP Tower, the office block in Paris's La Defense business district, was sold for 531 million francs to the Paul Doumer firm in 1988. It was sold again two years later for 1.1 billion francs ($192 million).

In a related legal action, BP France has sued Schwartz, Llewellyn, Michelon and Gatrill for 72.5 million francs ($12.6 million), a sum it says it would have earned from the sale had it gone through without alleged bribery.
